beats.lead: The story goes that East Germany decided to open the Berlin Wall
beats.text: It didn't. One man's mistake at a press conference did.
beats.note: On 9 November 1989, a Politburo spokesman was handed a note on new travel rules minutes before facing reporters, with no time to be briefed on it properly.

beats.name: Günter Schabowski
beats.role: East German Politburo spokesman. Read from a note he barely understood, live, in front of the world's press.

beats.lead: A reporter asked the obvious question
beats.note: Schabowski shuffled his papers, looked uncertain, then said: 'As far as I know — immediately, without delay.' The rules weren't due to start until 4am the next morning.

beats.lead: West German television broadcast it as fact
beats.text: By nightfall, thousands stood at the checkpoints demanding to cross.
beats.note: Border guards had no orders for this. No shots, no directive from above — just a crowd too large to hold back.

beats.text: At 11:30pm, a single guard at Bornholmer Straße opened the gate. Nobody above him had decided to.

beats.line: The Wall didn't fall by decision. It fell by mistake.
